note: Sat 21 Nov 2026 07:xx SGT run, as of the Fri 20 Nov US close (latest completed session; weekend, pre-Asia-Monday-open). Friday's AI-credibility shock (Nvidia SEC-probe report, Broadcom/Google TPU-order cut) dominates; several items are from the Nov 19-20 window specifically because that is when the news broke, not a freshness gap.

items.headline: Reuters: SEC enforcement staff examining Nvidia's accounting practices; shares fall ~14%, erasing ~$500bn
items.summary: Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining Nvidia's accounting practices, though the scope and start date were undisclosed. Shares fell as much as 14% intraday, the stock's worst session in years, acting as the single largest catalyst behind Friday's broad market selloff.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but this is the hardest-to-dismiss AI-capex-credibility shock of the drawdown -- watch for contagion into HK tech's own AI-capex narrative (0700.HK, 0981.HK) when Monday's Asia session opens and finally prices this in.

items.headline: Google reportedly cuts 2027 Broadcom TPU orders ~20% in favor of MediaTek; Broadcom -11.4%, Marvell -10%
items.summary: TF International analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reported Alphabet cut roughly 1 million units (~20%) of Broadcom-designed TPU 8i chips planned for 2027, reallocating to MediaTek-built TPU 8t chips, citing power and supply-chain constraints.
items.actionable: Concrete, sourced evidence that AI capex plans are being actively reshuffled, not just questioned in the abstract -- a second independent data point alongside the Nvidia probe for gauging how durable the 'AI winter' narrative is before adding risk anywhere in the book.

items.headline: Friday's selloff landed on monthly options expiration with ~55-57% of SPY/QQQ's negative gamma rolling off
items.summary: SpotGamma noted SPX net gamma was roughly -$137bn per 1% move at Thursday's close, with the bulk of SPY's and QQQ's 40-day negative gamma expiring Friday -- a structural setup that mechanically amplifies whatever directional news hits that day.
items.actionable: Explains why VIX's 26.2% spike to 35.89 was disproportionate even to the S&P's -3.70% move; argues against mechanically extrapolating Friday's magnitude into next week once gamma normalizes post-expiry.

items.headline: Gold/silver selloff diagnosed as a margin-call cascade, not a fresh bear catalyst -- directly relevant to the owner's levered silver position
items.summary: Analysts (Peter Schiff, Commerzbank, XTB) attribute the metals slide to leveraged investors raising cash from liquid winners (gold/silver) to meet equity-related margin calls; COMEX managed-money futures positions shrank even as ETF holdings rose, a classic forced-liquidation signature. Miners underperformed on operating leverage.
items.actionable: The single most important item for the owner's 2.487x-levered silver/miners position: a 'margin-call, not fundamental-bear' framing argues the move could partially mean-revert if equities stabilize, but the FAILING survivability metric means the owner is exposed to being forced-sold in exactly this dynamic before any reversion happens.

items.headline: Gold/silver ratio blows out to ~82-83, highest since Nov 2025, as silver ETF flows turn to outflow
items.summary: Metals Focus expects a 2026 silver ETF outflow of ~45m oz after a 278m oz inflow in 2025; the gold/silver ratio rose from ~78 (9 Nov) to ~83 (18 Nov), reflecting silver's steeper decline (down over 21% in the past month vs gold's smaller fall).
items.actionable: Confirms silver-specific (not just gold) forced de-risking is still running -- directly relevant to the owner's silver-heavy, leveraged book; the ratio blowout is a classic capitulation signature worth tracking for a potential reversal entry once margin pressure exhausts.

items.headline: Bitcoin's multi-week slide continues via ETF outflows, MSCI's removal of Strategy (MSTR), and weekend Coinbase-concentrated selling
items.summary: US spot BTC ETFs show roughly $1.9bn of cumulative outflows through mid-Nov; MSCI's Nov 11 decision to remove Strategy (holder of 850,364 BTC) from its global indexes by Nov 30 pressures sentiment; Coinbase alone accounted for ~$1.08bn of net BTC selling Oct 31-Nov 15, concentrated over weekends when liquidity is thinnest.
items.actionable: Friday's -4.51% BTC move and continued weekend softness look like a continuation of this multi-week structural drain rather than a new Friday-specific shock -- worth tracking as 'known, multi-week driver' distinct from the equity-market AI shock.

items.headline: Rare-earth basket round-trips: William Blair's USA Rare Earth downgrade, a 3-day relief rally, then Friday's broad reversal
items.summary: William Blair downgraded USA Rare Earth (USAR) on Nov 16-17 citing dysprosium/samarium feedstock shortages pushing estimates into 2028; USAR fell ~10-11.6%, Critical Metals -13%, MP Materials -5%. By Nov 18-19 the group rebounded 3-8% on US-China rare-earth-talk optimism before Friday's broad risk-off erased those gains (MP -7.39%).
items.actionable: Confirms MP's Friday decline was a broad-market/risk-off reversal of a rare-earth-specific relief rally, not a new MP-specific negative catalyst -- the underlying feedstock-delay bear case (USAR-specific) is a separate, slower-moving risk from Friday's macro-driven reversal.

items.headline: Fed Governor Waller renews push for a 50bp December hike, says Fed may need to 'shock' inflation expectations lower
items.summary: Waller told CNBC that stubborn ~3% inflation may require a jumbo hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC rather than 25bp, to prevent inflation expectations from becoming anchored too high; CME FedWatch still shows 25bp favored at roughly 90-97% odds vs 3-10% for 50bp.
items.actionable: Directly threatens the owner's SGX REITs via financing costs and adds a second, independent leg of pressure on silver/miners via the real-rate/dollar channel -- raises the probability December brings a genuine hawkish surprise, not just a priced-in 25bp.

items.headline: Final November UoM consumer sentiment revised up to 51.5; inflation expectations fall -- but gold fell anyway
items.summary: Final November reading rose to 51.5 (from October's 48.0), driven by post-midterm-election optimism; 1-year inflation expectations fell to 3.7% (from 4.7%) and 5-year to 3.3% (from 3.5%). Gold still fell roughly 3.67% that session, overwhelmed by equity-driven margin selling.
items.actionable: Confirms Friday's gold/silver weakness was NOT about inflation-expectations repricing (those improved) -- it was forced/margin selling, which matters for distinguishing a 'buy the dip' vs 'structural bear' read on the owner's heavily levered silver book.

items.headline: Tencent Q3 capex surges 225% YoY to RMB65.1bn amid AI buildout; president says US chip curbs delay next model
items.summary: Tencent's Q3 2026 results showed revenue +7.5-8% YoY to RMB207.3bn alongside a 225% YoY capex surge; President Martin Lau said new US curbs on offshore AI chip access 'set everyone back in China' and will delay Tencent's next model version.
items.actionable: Tencent's own AI-capex anxiety (echoing the global Nvidia/Broadcom theme) plus explicit commentary on US chip-export curbs hurting Chinese model development directly explains part of the HK session's weakness and is a read-through for the 0700.HK holding on both capex-sustainability and export-control fronts.

items.headline: Hang Seng closes -1.89% at 22,410.80, a 4th straight loss; Hang Seng Tech -3.78%, an 8th straight decline
items.summary: The weekly loss reached 5.19% (Hang Seng Tech -7.92%); SMIC and Hua Hong bucked the index trend intraday on continued China chip-self-sufficiency optimism following strong Q3 results, even as the broader tech complex extended its losing streak amid AI-spending-return skepticism.
items.actionable: Confirms HK's Friday session was already a multi-day losing streak before Friday's fresh US AI shock -- Monday's HK open is the first chance to price in the Nvidia/Broadcom news directly, so expect continued pressure on 0700/0981/1810.HK into next week.

items.headline: Singapore STI falls 2.07% to 4,974.43, a 5th straight session, as new US AI-chip export curbs hit local data centres
items.summary: DBS -2.31% to S$67.70, OCBC -2.23% to S$27.68, UOB -1.82% to S$36.70 as new US AI-chip export restrictions were reported to affect Singapore-based data centres, compounding the broader risk-off.
items.actionable: A concrete, Singapore-specific catalyst (AI chip export curbs hitting local data-center buildout) beyond generic global risk-off -- directly relevant to the owner's SGX banks/REITs/developers exposure and worth flagging as a new, distinct regional risk thread rather than just imported US weakness.

items.headline: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral in Shenzhen produces a joint declaration on oil supply and UN reform -- markets cratered the next day anyway
items.summary: The first-ever three-way meeting of the US, China and Russian leaders occurred on the sidelines of APEC China 2026; the three agreed to pursue expanded oil production and discuss UN reform, with Trump calling it a '12 out of 10.'
items.actionable: A genuinely de-escalatory geopolitical headline that did NOT prevent Friday's crater -- underscores that Friday's selloff was AI/credit-specific, not geopolitical risk-off, and is consistent with oil's relative flatness in the price spine (WTI +0.49%).

items.headline: Russia-Ukraine escalation runs in parallel to the Shenzhen summit: Crimea bridge strike retaliation, Kyiv embassy drone damage, Poland airspace violation
items.summary: Following a Ukrainian strike on the Kerch/Crimea bridge, Putin ended the Black Sea/energy-infrastructure strike moratorium; Russian drone/missile attacks on Kyiv damaged the Dutch and Austrian embassies; Poland's defense minister said Russia violated its airspace overnight with two missiles and a drone.
items.actionable: A genuine escalation running in parallel to the Trump-Xi-Putin 'de-escalation' headline, creating a confusing two-track geopolitical picture -- worth watching as a tail risk for HK tech/SGX exposure given regional spillover potential, though it does not appear to be Friday's proximate equity-selloff driver.
